query: I've got a 150-row table of device_type (mobile/desktop/tablet) against support_outcome (resolved/escalated/abandoned). I computed mutual information and got 0.42 nats — is that a real association or am I fooling myself with so few rows per cell?

Can you explain how cross-entropy loss, negative log-likelihood, and KL divergence are all the same thing? My DS lead keeps using them interchangeably and I want to know if that's actually correct or sloppy.

My variational inference posterior keeps coming out way too confident — the credible intervals are visibly too narrow compared to the MCMC run. Is this an optimization bug or something more fundamental about the objective?
We're estimating that our event-log stream is about 1.18 bits per character. How compressible does that make it, realistically, and what's the theoretical floor I should expect a compressor to hit?

Model A has 9 parameters, model B has 5. AIC slightly prefers A, BIC clearly prefers B. Which one do I actually report in the paper, and how do I justify the choice rather than just picking the one I like?
I computed the differential entropy of one of my continuous features and got -2.4. A negative entropy seems like it has to be a bug — what did I do wrong?
What's the KL divergence between N(0,1) and N(2,3), and does it matter which way round I put them? I always forget whether KL is symmetric.

I ranked all 180 of my candidate features by mutual information with the churn label and kept the top 25. A teammate says MI ranking is biased and I'm probably keeping a bunch of redundant high-cardinality junk. Is she right?

My decision tree's first split is on customer_id and it gets near-perfect information gain on training data. Obviously something is wrong but I want to understand exactly why the split criterion is rewarding this.

For a biodiversity side project I sampled 30 individuals across species and want a single number for how diverse the community is. People mention a 'diversity index' — how do I compute it and what are the gotchas with so few individuals?

I have a set of RR interval series from a wearable study and want to compute the sample entropy of each one (m=2, r=0.2*SD). Can you sanity-check my approach and tell me how to read the numbers across participants?

I want to quantify how complex / unpredictable an EEG channel is. Which 'entropy' is the right one here — I keep seeing sample entropy, permutation entropy, and plain Shannon entropy thrown around and I don't know which applies.
My PyTorch training crashes with 'Expected target size [32, 10], got [32]' on nn.CrossEntropyLoss. How do I fix the tensor shapes I'm passing to the loss?
I'm redesigning the navigation for our docs site and want help with the information architecture — how to group the sections and label the top-level menu so people can find things.
Can you explain the second law of thermodynamics and why entropy always increases in an isolated system? Trying to refresh my undergrad physics.
I have about $40k in a taxable brokerage and I'm trying to decide between a total-market index fund and a target-date fund. Which makes more sense for a long horizon?
I need to compress about 200 PDFs so I can email them — they're too big for the attachment limit. What's the easiest way to zip and shrink them on my Mac?
I have log lines like 'epoch=12 H=3.41 bits loss=0.88'. Write me a regex to pull out the number after 'H=' so I can plot it.
My random forest's feature_importances_ change a lot between runs and even reorder the top features. How do I get a more stable importance ranking?
I'm reading a trajectory-optimization paper that uses the 'cross-entropy method' to sample action sequences for model-predictive control. Can you walk me through how that CEM update loop works?

Our team keeps talking about 'entropy' in the codebase — meaning the accumulating tech debt and dead code that makes everything harder to change. Any strategies for measuring and reducing that kind of software rot?
I ran an A/B test on the new onboarding flow: 4.1% vs 4.6% conversion over two weeks. Is that difference significant at the 0.05 level, and how should I set up the test?
How many survey respondents do I need to estimate our top-task completion rate within +/- 3 percentage points? Trying to figure out the sample size before we field it.
I want the power spectrum of an accelerometer signal — just the FFT magnitude across frequency bands so I can see which rhythms dominate. What's the cleanest way to compute and plot that?

I've got two coupled sensor time series and I want to figure out which one is driving the other — the relationship looks nonlinear so I don't think a plain VAR will cut it. What's the right information-theoretic measure and how do I keep it from giving me spurious directionality?

I have a zero-mean Gaussian-ish signal and I need to know the minimum number of bits per sample to store it if I can tolerate a certain mean-squared error. Is there a clean formula for the bits-vs-fidelity tradeoff?

My event-log stream has strong sequential structure. If I want the true per-symbol information content — not just the entropy of how often each event type shows up — how do I compute that, and why are the two different?

Before I spend another week tuning models: given that the mutual information between my features and the label is only about 1.5 bits for a 10-class problem, is there a hard floor on the error rate that no classifier can beat?

My classifier's log-loss is really low and my PM wants to show the predicted probabilities to users as confidence scores. Is a low log-loss enough to trust that those probabilities are actually calibrated?
What's the cleanest tool or codec to compress a folder of 4K video files for archiving? I care about file size vs visible quality but I just want a practical recommendation, not theory.
How do I do post-training int8 quantization of my PyTorch model so it runs faster on edge devices? Looking for the API and a code snippet.
Can you give me a short history of Claude Shannon and how information theory got started? It's for a talk intro, just the story and the people.
I have a 2x2 contingency table with small counts and want to test for association. How do I compute a Fisher exact test p-value in scipy?
My smartwatch says my heart rate variability has been low for a few weeks and I'm worried it means something is wrong with my health. Should I be concerned?
